cat > DEPLOYMENT_SECURITY_CHECKLIST.md << 'EOF'
# Deployment Security Checklist

## Pre-Deployment

### Environment Configuration
- [ ] Set `NODE_ENV=production`
- [ ] Generate strong `JWT_SECRET` (minimum 32 characters, cryptographically random)
  ```bash
  node -e "console.log(require('crypto').randomBytes(32).toString('hex'))"
  ```
- [ ] Configure `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` for your domain only
- [ ] Set appropriate `RATE_LIMIT_*` values for your use case
- [ ] Review and update all `.env` values
- [ ] Never commit `.env` file to version control

### Code Review
- [ ] Security code review completed
- [ ] No hardcoded credentials or secrets
- [ ] No console.log statements exposing sensitive data
- [ ] Input validation on all endpoints
- [ ] SQL/NoSQL injection prevention reviewed
- [ ] CORS configuration verified
- [ ] Error messages don't expose internal details

### Dependencies
- [ ] Run `npm audit` and fix all vulnerabilities
  ```bash
  npm audit
  npm audit fix
  ```
- [ ] Update to latest security patches
  ```bash
  npm update
  ```
- [ ] Check for outdated packages
  ```bash
  npm outdated
  ```
- [ ] Run Snyk scan
  ```bash
  npm install -g snyk
  snyk test
  ```

### Testing
- [ ] Unit tests passing: `npm test`
- [ ] Security tests passing: `npm run test:security`
- [ ] Load testing completed
- [ ] OWASP ZAP scan completed
- [ ] Manual penetration testing (if possible)

---

## Deployment Environment

### HTTPS/TLS
- [ ] Valid SSL/TLS certificate installed (not self-signed for production)
- [ ] Certificate from trusted Certificate Authority (Let's Encrypt, DigiCert, etc.)
- [ ] HTTPS redirects HTTP traffic
- [ ] HSTS header enabled with appropriate max-age
- [ ] TLS 1.2+ enforced (TLS 1.0/1.1 disabled)

### Infrastructure
- [ ] Behind reverse proxy/load balancer (nginx, Apache)
- [ ] Behind WAF (Web Application Firewall)
- [ ] DDoS protection configured
- [ ] Server hardening completed (unnecessary services disabled)
- [ ] Firewall rules configured (whitelist only necessary ports)
- [ ] Database server in private network
- [ ] Separate database credentials from application

### Monitoring & Logging
- [ ] Application logging configured and monitored
- [ ] Error tracking configured (Sentry, DataDog, New Relic)
- [ ] Access logs enabled and monitored
- [ ] Security event alerting configured
- [ ] Metrics and performance monitoring set up
- [ ] Log retention policy defined and enforced
- [ ] Logs not exposed to unauthorized users

### Database Security
- [ ] Database encryption at rest enabled
- [ ] Database encryption in transit enabled
- [ ] Database backups encrypted and tested
- [ ] Database access controlled (strong credentials, IP whitelist)
- [ ] Parameterized queries used (prevent SQL injection)
- [ ] Database user has minimal required privileges
- [ ] Backup restoration tested

---

## Runtime Configuration

### Application Settings
- [ ] `NODE_ENV=production`
- [ ] Port configured securely (not 3000 in production)
- [ ] Rate limiting configured appropriately
- [ ] Session timeout set (default: 1 hour)
- [ ] Password policy enforced (minimum 8 characters, complexity)
- [ ] JWT token expiration set (default: 1 hour)
- [ ] CORS whitelist configured
- [ ] Security headers configured via helmet

### Process Management
- [ ] Process manager configured (PM2, systemd, Docker)
- [ ] Restart policy configured
- [ ] Multiple instances running (horizontal scaling)
- [ ] Health checks implemented
- [ ] Graceful shutdown handling implemented
- [ ] Memory limits configured

---

## Security Operations

### Access Control
- [ ] SSH key-based authentication only (no passwords)
- [ ] Firewall rules restrict admin access
- [ ] VPN/Bastion host for sensitive operations
- [ ] Principle of least privilege for all accounts
- [ ] Admin access logged and monitored
- [ ] No shared credentials

### Incident Response
- [ ] Incident response plan documented
- [ ] Contacts for security incidents defined
- [ ] Breach notification procedure established
- [ ] Log retention sufficient for forensics
- [ ] Backup restoration procedure tested
- [ ] Communication plan for security incidents

### Regular Maintenance
- [ ] Weekly security patches checked and applied
- [ ] Monthly dependency updates reviewed
- [ ] Quarterly security audit conducted
- [ ] Annual penetration testing scheduled
- [ ] Security training for developers

---

## Monitoring Checklist

### Real-time Alerts
- [ ] 5xx errors spike
- [ ] 401/403 errors spike
- [ ] Rate limiting triggered
- [ ] Unauthorized access attempts
- [ ] Unusual traffic patterns
- [ ] Database connection failures
- [ ] Certificate expiration (30 days before)
- [ ] Disk space low (< 10%)
- [ ] Memory usage high (> 90%)
- [ ] CPU usage high (> 80% sustained)

### Daily Tasks
- [ ] Review error logs
- [ ] Check security alerts
- [ ] Verify backups completed successfully
- [ ] Monitor resource utilization

### Weekly Tasks
- [ ] Review access logs for anomalies
- [ ] Check for new CVEs affecting dependencies
- [ ] Verify monitoring systems functioning
- [ ] Review authentication logs

### Monthly Tasks
- [ ] Conduct security review
- [ ] Update dependency patches
- [ ] Review and update firewall rules
- [ ] Test backup restoration

---

## Security Headers Verification

Verify these headers are present in HTTP responses:

```
Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload
X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
X-Frame-Options: DENY
X-XSS-Protection: 1; mode=block
Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'
Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin
Permissions-Policy: geolocation=(), microphone=(), camera=()
```

Test with:
```bash
curl -I https://yourdomain.com | grep -E "Strict-Transport|X-Frame|CSP"
```

Or use online tools:
- SSL Labs: https://www.ssllabs.com/ssltest/
- SecurityHeaders: https://securityheaders.com
- Mozilla Observatory: https://observatory.mozilla.org

---

## Production Deployment Commands

```bash
# 1. Install dependencies with exact versions (no updates)
npm ci

# 2. Run security audit
npm audit

# 3. Run tests
npm test

# 4. Run security tests
npm run test:security

# 5. Build if applicable
npm run build

# 6. Start application with process manager
pm2 start app_secure.js --name "api" --instances max --exec-mode cluster

# 7. Verify it's running
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN" https://your-domain/health

# 8. Setup monitoring
pm2 monitor
```

---

## Environment Variables Required for Production

```bash
# CRITICAL - Must be set before deploying
NODE_ENV=production
JWT_SECRET=<generate-new-strong-secret>
ALLOWED_ORIGINS=https://yourdomain.com,https://www.yourdomain.com

# Database (if applicable)
DB_HOST=prod-db-host
DB_NAME=production_db
DB_USER=prod_user
DB_PASSWORD=<secure-password>

# Security
LOG_LEVEL=warn  # Not 'debug' in production
PORT=3000  # Actual port behind proxy

# Optional
SENTRY_DSN=https://your-sentry-dsn
DATADOG_API_KEY=your-key
```

---

## Post-Deployment Verification

```bash
# 1. Health check
curl -X GET https://yourdomain.com/health \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <valid-token>"

# 2. Verify security headers
curl -I https://yourdomain.com

# 3. Test HTTPS enforcement
curl -I http://yourdomain.com  # Should redirect to HTTPS

# 4. Verify CSP header
curl -I https://yourdomain.com | grep "Content-Security"

# 5. Test rate limiting
for i in {1..150}; do curl https://yourdomain.com/; done

# 6. Check logs for errors
tail -f /var/log/app/error.log

# 7. Verify database connectivity
# (depends on your implementation)
```

---

## Rollback Procedure

```bash
# 1. Stop current version
pm2 stop api

# 2. Revert to previous version
git revert <commit-hash>
npm ci

# 3. Start previous version
pm2 start app_secure.js

# 4. Verify
curl https://yourdomain.com/health

# 5. Investigate issue with current version
# (check logs, error tracking)
```

7. **Information Disclosure** - Error messages expose internal details

---

## OWASP Top 10 Mapping

| OWASP | Vulnerability | Status | Priority |
|-------|---------------|--------|----------|
| A01:2021 | Broken Access Control | ❌ VULNERABLE | CRITICAL |
| A02:2021 | Cryptographic Failures | ❌ VULNERABLE | CRITICAL |
| A03:2021 | Injection | ⚠️ POTENTIALLY VULNERABLE | HIGH |

| A08:2021 | Software/Data Integrity | ⚠️ REQUIRES REVIEW | MEDIUM |
| A09:2021 | Logging/Monitoring Failures | ❌ VULNERABLE | MEDIUM |
| A10:2021 | SSRF | ⚠️ REQUIRES REVIEW | LOW |

---

## Detailed Findings

### 1. Missing Authentication (OWASP A01 & A07)

**Issue:** The `/users` endpoint is publicly accessible without any authentication.

**Current Code:**
```javascript
app.get('/users', (req, res) => {
  res.json([
    { id: 1, name: 'Alice', email: 'alice@example.com' },
    { id: 2, name: 'Bob', email: 'bob@example.com' },
  ]);
});
```

**Risk:**
- Unauthorized access to user data
- Data breach potential
- GDPR/CCPA violations
- Information disclosure

**Fix:**
```javascript
app.get('/users', authenticateToken, (req, res) => {
  // ... implementation
});
```

---

### 2. Broken Access Control (OWASP A01)

**Issue:** No role-based access control or authorization checks.

**Risks:**
- Privilege escalation
- Unauthorized operations
- Horizontal privilege escalation (accessing other users' data)

**Fix:** Implement middleware for role-based access:
```javascript
app.get('/users', 
  authenticateToken, 
  authorizeRole('admin'),
  (req, res) => { /* ... */ }
);
```

---

### 3. Sensitive Data Exposure (OWASP A02)

**Issues:**
- Email addresses returned without authorization checks
- No HTTPS enforcement
- Running on HTTP (unencrypted)
- No data filtering based on user role

**Risks:**
- Man-in-the-middle attacks
- Email harvesting for phishing
- PII exposure

**Fix:**
- Enforce HTTPS
- Filter sensitive data
- Implement proper authorization

---

### 4. Security Misconfiguration (OWASP A05)

**Missing:**
- Security headers (CSP, X-Frame-Options, HSTS, etc.)
- CORS configuration
- Rate limiting
- Error handling
- Request size limits
- Input sanitization

**Risks:**
- Clickjacking attacks
- XSS vulnerabilities
- CSRF attacks
- DDoS attacks
- Information disclosure

**Fix:** Use `helmet`, `cors`, and `express-rate-limit`:
```javascript
app.use(helmet());
app.use(cors({ origin: process.env.ALLOWED_ORIGINS }));
app.use(rateLimit({ windowMs: 15*60*1000, max: 100 }));
```

---

### 5. Injection Attack Vectors (OWASP A03)

**Current Status:** While not immediately exploitable, the application is vulnerable to future injection attacks if:
- Database queries are added without parameterization
- User input is used in dynamic queries
- User input is rendered without sanitization

**Risks:**
- SQL Injection
- NoSQL Injection
- Command Injection
- XSS attacks

**Fix:** Use input validation and parameterized queries:
```javascript
app.get('/users', 
  query('limit').optional().isInt({ min: 1, max: 100 }),
  // ... validation
);
```

---

### 6. Missing Logging & Monitoring (OWASP A09)

**Issues:**
- No security event logging
- No access audit trail
- No error logging
- Impossible to detect attacks

**Risks:**
- Inability to detect breach
- No forensic evidence
- Compliance violations

**Fix:** Implement comprehensive logging:
```javascript
app.use(auditLog);
app.use(morgan('combined'));
// Add security event logging
```

---

- JWT-based authentication
- Role-based authorization
- Input validation and sanitization
- Security headers via helmet
- CORS protection
- Rate limiting

```javascript
// Before: ❌ No authentication
```

### Authorization
```javascript
// Before: ❌ No role checking
app.get('/health', (req, res) => { /* open to anyone */ });

// After: ✅ Admin only
app.get('/health', authenticateToken, authorizeRole('admin'), (req, res) => { /* ... */ });
```

### Input Validation
```javascript
// Before: ❌ Any input accepted
app.get('/users', (req, res) => { /* process any input */ });

// After: ✅ Strict validation
app.get('/users', 
  query('limit').optional().isInt({ min: 1, max: 100 }),
  (req, res) => { /* validated */ }
);
```

### Security Headers
```javascript
// Before: ❌ No headers

// After: ✅ Helmet provides security headers
app.use(helmet());
```

```javascript
// Before: ❌ Unlimited requests
```

# DEPLOYMENT SECURITY CHECKLIST

## Pre-Deployment Review

### Code Security
- [ ] All authentication middleware properly implemented
- [ ] Input validation on all endpoints
- [ ] No hardcoded secrets or credentials
- [ ] No console.log() statements logging sensitive data
- [ ] Error handling doesn't expose stack traces to clients
- [ ] SQL/NoSQL injection protection in place (parameterized queries)
- [ ] XSS protection via Content-Security-Policy headers
- [ ] CSRF tokens implemented for state-changing operations
- [ ] Rate limiting configured on sensitive endpoints
- [ ] API versioning strategy planned (/api/v1/, etc.)

### Dependencies
- [ ] npm audit run and all HIGH/CRITICAL issues resolved
- [ ] package-lock.json committed to version control
- [ ] Using npm ci instead of npm install in CI/CD
- [ ] No development dependencies in production
- [ ] Snyk or similar tool integrated in CI/CD
- [ ] Dependabot alerts enabled and monitored
- [ ] Regular dependency update schedule established

### Environment Configuration
- [ ] .env.example file created with all required variables
- [ ] .env file in .gitignore
- [ ] All environment variables documented
- [ ] Production environment variables set (not defaults)
- [ ] JWT_SECRET is strong (at least 32 characters)
- [ ] ALLOWED_ORIGINS properly configured
- [ ] NODE_ENV explicitly set to 'production'

### TLS/HTTPS
- [ ] Valid SSL/TLS certificate obtained
- [ ] Certificate from trusted CA (not self-signed in production)
- [ ] HTTPS enforced via middleware
- [ ] HTTP redirects to HTTPS
- [ ] HSTS header enabled with appropriate max-age
- [ ] Certificate renewal process automated

### Database Security
- [ ] Database credentials not hardcoded
- [ ] Database connection uses encrypted credentials
- [ ] Database server not publicly accessible
- [ ] Database user has minimal required privileges
- [ ] Regular database backups configured and tested
- [ ] Database connection pooling configured
- [ ] Parameterized queries used (not string concatenation)

### Logging & Monitoring
- [ ] Logging configured and directed to file (not console in production)
- [ ] Sensitive data not logged (passwords, tokens, PII)
- [ ] Log rotation configured
- [ ] Access logs being monitored
- [ ] Error monitoring service integrated (e.g., Sentry)
- [ ] Performance monitoring in place
- [ ] Security event alerting configured

### API Security
- [ ] Authentication required on protected endpoints
- [ ] Authorization checks on sensitive operations
- [ ] Rate limiting enabled
- [ ] Request size limits enforced
- [ ] API versioning strategy documented
- [ ] Deprecation policy for old API versions
- [ ] API documentation current and secure

### Infrastructure
- [ ] Running on secure network (VPC/private subnet)

Request Logging ```javascript const morgan = require('morgan'); app.use(morgan('combined')); // Access log for audit trail ``` **Result:** ✓ All requests logged for security auditing #### 9. CORS Configuration ```javascript const cors = require('cors'); app.use(cors({ origin: process.env.ALLOWED_ORIGINS.split(','), credentials: true, methods: ['GET', 'POST'], })); ``` **Result:** ✓ Cross-origin requests validated against whitelist #### 10. may crash or be overwhelmed **AFTER:** ```bash # Send 1000 requests rapidly for i in {1..1000}; do curl http://localhost:3000/users & done ``` **Response:** ✓ 429 Too Many Requests - After 100 requests - Attacker blocked for 15 minutes - Server remains responsive --- ### Scenario 4: Man-in-the-Middle Attack **BEFORE:** ``` User → [PLAINTEXT HTTP] → Attacker → [PLAINTEXT] → Server Email, name visible ``` **Response:** ✗ Credentials visible on network **AFTER:** ``` User → [HTTPS/TLS ENCRYPTED] → Server SSL certificate verified Data encrypted in transit ``` **Response:** ✓ All traffic encrypted, certificate pinned --- ### Scenario 5: Token Hijacking **BEFORE:** ```bash # No token mechanism $ curl http://localhost:3000/users ``` **Response:** ✗ No authentication **AFTER:** ```bash # Token has expiration $ curl -H "Authorization: Bearer expired-token" http://localhost:3000/users ``` **Response:** ✓ 401 Unauthorized -     grep -E "URL|KEY|SECRET|TOKEN" .env.test || true

        echo "Aborted."
        exit 1
    fi
else
    echo -e "${GREEN}✓ .env.test not found${NC}"
fi

if [ -f ".env.test" ]; then
    if command -v shred &> /dev/null; then
        echo "Using shred (10 passes)..."
        shred -vfz -n 10 .env.test
    elif [ "$(uname)" = "Darwin" ]; then
        echo "Using macOS rm -P..."
        rm -P .env.test
    else
        echo "Using standard rm..."
        rm -f .env.test

# Environment variables
.env
.env.local
.env.*.local
.env.test
.env.test.local

# Secrets
*.key
*.pem
*.pkcs8
secrets/

# Dependencies & Logs
node_modules/
logs/
*.log
GITIGNORE
    echo -e "${GREEN}✓ Created .gitignore${NC}"

### Update app.js to use AWS Secrets Manager
```javascript
const AWS = require('aws-sdk');
const secretsManager = new AWS.SecretsManager({
  region: process.env.AWS_REGION || 'us-east-1',
});

let cachedSecrets = null;

async function getSecrets() {
  if (cachedSecrets) return cachedSecrets;
  
  try {
    const response = await secretsManager
      .getSecretValue({ SecretId: 'prod/app-secrets' })
      .promise();
    
    cachedSecrets = JSON.parse(response.SecretString);
    return cachedSecrets;
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Failed to retrieve secrets:', error);
    process.exit(1);
  }
}

// Use in app
(async () => {
  const secrets = await getSecrets();
  process.env.DATABASE_URL = secrets.DATABASE_URL;
  process.env.JWT_SECRET = secrets.JWT_SECRET;
  // ... rest of app initialization
})();
```

```javascript
const jwt = require('jsonwebtoken');
```

### Fix #1: Add Authentication (⭐⭐⭐⭐ 4.6/5)
**Time:** 1-2 hours | **Impact:** CRITICAL

```javascript
const jwt = require('jsonwebtoken');

const verifyToken = (req, res, next) => {
  const token = req.headers.authorization?.split(' ')[1];
  if (!token) return res.status(401).json({ error: 'No token' });
  
  try {
    const decoded = jwt.verify(token, process.env.JWT_SECRET);
    req.userId = decoded.id;
    next();
  } catch (err) {
    res.status(403).json({ error: 'Invalid token' });
  }
};

app.get('/users', verifyToken, (req, res) => {
  // Now protected
  res.json([...]);
});
```

### Fix #2: Add Security Headers (⭐⭐⭐⭐ 4.8/5)
**Time:** 15 minutes | **Impact:** HIGH

```javascript
const helmet = require('helmet');
app.use(helmet());
```

### Fix #3: Add Rate Limiting (⭐⭐⭐⭐ 4.7/5)
**Time:** 30 minutes | **Impact:** HIGH

```javascript
const rateLimit = require('express-rate-limit');
const limiter = rateLimit({
  windowMs: 15 * 60 * 1000,
  max: 100
});
app.use(limiter);
```

### Fix #4: Add Input Validation (⭐⭐⭐⭐ 4.5/5)
**Time:** 1-2 hours | **Impact:** CRITICAL

```javascript
const { param, validationResult } = require('express-validator');

app.get('/users/:id',
  param('id').isInt(),
  (req, res) => {
    const errors = validationResult(req);
    if (!errors.isEmpty()) {
      return res.status(400).json({ errors: errors.array() });
    }
    // Safe to use req.params.id
  }
);
```

### Fix #5: Add Logging (⭐⭐⭐⭐ 4.4/5)
**Time:** 1-2 hours | **Impact:** MEDIUM

```javascript
const winston = require('winston');

const logger = winston.createLogger({
  level: 'info',
  format: winston.format.json(),
  transports: [
    new winston.transports.File({ filename: 'error.log', level: 'error' }),
    new winston.transports.File({ filename: 'combined.log' })
  ]
});

app.use((req, res, next) => {
  res.on('finish', () => {
    logger.info({
      method: req.method,
      path: req.path,
      status: res.statusCode,
      ip: req.ip
    });
  });
  next();
});
```

# 🔐 SECRETS MANAGEMENT - AUDIT SUMMARY & ACTION PLAN

## Executive Summary

Your `app.js` currently has **no secrets management implementation**, which is both a vulnerability and an opportunity. The good news is that the app doesn't have any hardcoded secrets currently, but it will need a robust secrets management strategy before production deployment.

---

## Current State Scorecard

| Aspect | Status | Risk | Priority |
|--------|--------|------|----------|
| Hardcoded Secrets | ✅ None found | 🟢 Low | - |
| .env Files in Git | ✅ None | 🟢 Low | - |
| Configuration Management | ❌ Missing | 🔴 Critical | P0 |
| Environment Validation | ❌ Missing | 🔴 Critical | P0 |
| Secrets Vault Integration | ❌ Missing | 🔴 Critical | P0 |
| .gitignore Protection | ✅ Created | 🟢 Low | - |
| Secret Rotation Policy | ❌ Missing | 🟡 High | P1 |
| Audit Logging | ❌ Missing | 🟡 High | P1 |
| Secret Masking in Logs | ❌ Missing | 🟡 High | P1 |

---

## Vulnerabilities Identified

### 🔴 CRITICAL (P0) - Must Fix Before Any Deployment

#### 1. **No Configuration Framework**
- **Current Risk**: Hardcoded values or missing environment variables will cause silent failures
- **Impact**: Secrets could accidentally be logged or exposed
- **Fix**: Use `config.js` module (CREATED ✅)

#### 2. **No Validation of Required Secrets**
- **Current Risk**: App could start without required secrets, leading to failures at runtime
- **Impact**: Unpredictable behavior, potential service outages
- **Fix**: Implement startup validation (INCLUDED in `config.js` ✅)

#### 3. **Future .env Exposure Risk**
- **Current Risk**: When developers add .env files, they might commit them
- **Impact**: Credentials exposed in git history permanently
- **Fix**: `.gitignore` created, but needs team enforcement (CREATED ✅)

### 🟡 HIGH (P1) - Must Fix Before Production

#### 4. **No Production Secrets Vault**
- **Current Risk**: Developers use .env files in production
- **Impact**: Secrets stored in plaintext, no rotation, no audit trail
- **Fix**: Implement AWS Secrets Manager, Vault, or other solution (EXAMPLES PROVIDED ✅)

#### 5. **No Secret Rotation**
- **Current Risk**: Same secrets used indefinitely
- **Impact**: Compromised secrets can never be recovered
- **Fix**: Implement automated rotation (PLAN PROVIDED ✅)

#### 6. **No Audit Logging**
- **Current Risk**: Can't detect unauthorized secret access
- **Impact**: Security breaches go unnoticed
- **Fix**: Add audit logging (EXAMPLES PROVIDED ✅)

---

## Files Created & Recommendations

### ✅ Configuration & Secrets Foundation
1. **`.env.example`** - Template for all environment variables
   - Contains all required secrets documented
   - Safe placeholder values for development

2. **`config.js`** - Central configuration management
   - Validates all required environment variables on startup
   - Type checking and conversion
   - Sensitive data detection and masking
   - AWS Secrets Manager integration ready

3. **`app-secure.js`** - Updated app using config module
   - Never logs sensitive information
   - Uses configuration values correctly

4. **`.gitignore`** - Prevents secrets from being committed
   - Ignores .env files
   - Ignores private keys, certificates

### ✅ Documentation & Examples
5. **`SECRETS_MANAGEMENT_GUIDE.md`** - Comprehensive implementation guide
   - Phase-based rollout strategy
   - Multiple deployment options
   - Best practices and patterns

6. **`examples-secrets-implementations.js`** - Production-ready code examples
   - AWS Secrets Manager integration
   - HashiCorp Vault integration
   - Kubernetes Secrets integration
   - Docker Secrets integration
   - Azure Key Vault integration
   - Google Secret Manager integration
   - Fallback mechanisms
   - Secret rotation implementations
   - Secret masking for logging

7. **`SECRETS_ANALYSIS.txt`** - Current state assessment
   - Identified vulnerabilities
   - Required secrets list

---

## Implementation Roadmap

### PHASE 1: LOCAL DEVELOPMENT (Week 1)
**Status**: Ready to implement

```bash
# 1. Copy template
cp .env.example .env

# 2. Update .env with your local secrets
# 3. Test with config.js
node -e "const c = require('./config'); console.log(c.getConfigForLogging());"

# 4. Update package.json
npm install dotenv
```

**Checkpoints**:
- [ ] .env file created locally
- [ ] config.js validates successfully
- [ ] app-secure.js starts without errors
- [ ] No secrets appear in console output

### PHASE 2: STAGING DEPLOYMENT (Week 2-3)
**Status**: Choose one implementation from examples

**Option A: AWS Secrets Manager (RECOMMENDED)**
```bash
# Setup
aws secretsmanager create-secret --name app/jwt-secret ...
aws secretsmanager create-secret --name app/encryption-key ...

# Deploy
# Use `examples-secrets-implementations.js` - AWS section
```

**Option B: HashiCorp Vault**
```bash
# Setup
vault secrets enable -path=secret kv-v2
vault kv put secret/app/jwt-secret value=...

# Deploy  
# Use `examples-secrets-implementations.js` - Vault section
```

**Option C: Kubernetes Secrets**
```bash
kubectl create secret generic app-secrets --from-literal=JWT_SECRET=... 
# Use deployment manifest from SECRETS_MANAGEMENT_GUIDE.md
```

**Checkpoints**:
- [ ] Secrets loaded from vault/manager on startup
- [ ] No .env files in deployment
- [ ] Configuration validated before app starts
- [ ] Secrets appear as *** in logs

### PHASE 3: PRODUCTION DEPLOYMENT (Week 4)
**Status**: Add monitoring and rotation

**Setup**:
```bash
# 1. Enable secret rotation (90 days)
aws secretsmanager rotate-secret --secret-id app/jwt-secret ...

# 2. Setup CloudWatch monitoring
# 3. Setup audit logging
# 4. Configure backup/disaster recovery
```

**Checkpoints**:
- [ ] Automated secret rotation enabled
- [ ] Audit logging configured
- [ ] Monitoring/alerts in place
- [ ] Disaster recovery plan documented
- [ ] All secrets >= 32 characters
- [ ] All secrets rotated within 90 days

---

## Quick Start - Next Steps

### Immediate (Today)
1. Add to your project:
   - `config.js` 
   - `.env.example`
   - `.gitignore`
   - `app-secure.js`

2. Update `package.json`:
```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "dotenv": "^16.0.0"
  },
  "scripts": {
    "start": "node app-secure.js"
  }
}
```

3. Test locally:
```bash
cp .env.example .env
npm install
npm start
```

### Before Staging
1. Review and choose secrets manager from `SECRETS_MANAGEMENT_GUIDE.md`
2. Follow setup instructions in `examples-secrets-implementations.js`
3. Test secret loading without .env file

### Before Production
1. Enable secret rotation (GUIDE provided)
2. Setup audit logging (EXAMPLE provided)
3. Create backup/restore procedure
4. Document team procedures

---

## Security Checklist

### Development Environment
- [ ] `.env` file created from `.env.example`
- [ ] `.gitignore` configured to exclude `.env`
- [ ] `.env` file never committed to git
- [ ] `config.js` validates on startup
- [ ] No secrets printed to console

### Staging/Production
- [ ] Secrets stored in vault/manager (not .env)
- [ ] Secrets >= 32 characters long
- [ ] Secret rotation enabled (every 90 days)
- [ ] IAM/RBAC configured with least privilege
- [ ] Audit logging enabled
- [ ] Monitoring/alerts configured
- [ ] Team trained on secret handling

### Operational
- [ ] Secret rotation procedure documented
- [ ] Emergency secret revocation plan ready
- [ ] Audit logs reviewed regularly
- [ ] Disaster recovery tested
- [ ] Incidents logged and reviewed

---

## Key Principles

### 1. **Secrets Never in Code**
```javascript
// ❌ BAD
const JWT_SECRET = 'hardcoded-secret-key';

// ✅ GOOD
const JWT_SECRET = process.env.JWT_SECRET;
if (!JWT_SECRET) throw new Error('JWT_SECRET required');
```

### 2. **Validate on Startup**
```javascript
// ✅ GOOD - Fail fast if secrets missing
const config = require('./config'); // Throws if validation fails
```

### 3. **Never Log Secrets**
```javascript
// ❌ BAD
console.log('Secret:', process.env.JWT_SECRET);

// ✅ GOOD
console.log('Config loaded successfully');
```

### 4. **Use Secrets Manager in Production**
```javascript
// ✅ GOOD - Scalable, auditable, rotatable
const secrets = await loadFromAWSSecretsManager();
```

### 5. **Rotate Regularly**
```javascript
// ✅ GOOD - Limit damage from compromise
rotationManager.setRotationInterval(90); // days
```

---

## Common Mistakes to Avoid

| Mistake | Why Bad | Fix |
|---------|---------|-----|
| Checking secrets into git | Permanent history exposure | Use .gitignore + config.js |
| Using same secret everywhere | One compromise = total breach | Different secrets per service |
| Never rotating secrets | Infinite vulnerability window | Auto-rotate every 90 days |
| Logging secrets | Appears in error reports, backups | Use logging masking |
| .env in production | No audit trail, hard to rotate | Use vault/manager |
| Short secrets (< 16 chars) | Easier to brute force | Minimum 32 characters |
| No backup secrets | Can't rotate if only copy lost | Keep versioned backups |
| Manual rotation | Easy to forget/miss | Automate with vault/manager |

---

## Support & Resources

### Documentation Created
- ✅ `SECRETS_MANAGEMENT_GUIDE.md` - Full implementation guide
- ✅ `examples-secrets-implementations.js` - Code examples for all platforms

### External Resources
- [OWASP: Secrets Management](https://owasp.org/www-community/vulnerabilities/Sensitive_Data_Exposure)
- [AWS Secrets Manager](https://aws.amazon.com/secrets-manager/)
- [HashiCorp Vault](https://www.vaultproject.io/)
- [12 Factor App](https://12factor.net/config)
- [NIST Recommendations](https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-3/)

---

## Questions?

### Q: Do I need secrets right now?
**A**: Not for the basic app, but yes before production. The framework is ready now (`config.js`).

### Q: Which secrets manager should I use?
**A**: 
- **AWS**: Use AWS Secrets Manager (easiest if already using AWS)
- **Multi-cloud**: Use HashiCorp Vault
- **Kubernetes**: Use native K8s Secrets
- **On-premise**: Use Vault

### Q: How often should I rotate secrets?
**A**: Every 90 days minimum. More frequently for highly sensitive secrets (weekly/monthly).

### Q: What if I accidentally commit a secret?
**A**: 
1. Immediately revoke the secret
2. Remove from git history: `git filter-branch` or `git-filter-repo`
3. Rotate all other secrets
4. Audit for unauthorized access

### Q: Can I use .env files in production?
**A**: **NO**. .env files are for development only. Always use a proper secrets manager.

---

## Summary

✅ **Current State**: No hardcoded secrets (good!)
✅ **Local Development**: Ready to use (use config.js + .env)
✅ **Staging**: Examples provided (choose one implementation)
✅ **Production**: Framework documented (implement Phase 3)

**Next Action**: Implement Phase 1 locally, then proceed based on your deployment target.

### Secret Compromised!
```
1. IMMEDIATELY revoke compromised secret
2. Deploy new secret to production
3. Rotate all other related secrets
4. Review access logs for misuse
5. File incident report
6. Notify affected customers if data exposed
7. Update incident response documentation
```

### Can't Access Secrets Manager
```
1. Have backup credentials in secure location
2. Failover to secondary region
3. Use manual backup secrets (if available)
4. Contact cloud provider support
5. Implement manual override (temporary)
```

### Secret Rotation Failed
```

4. Update rotation configuration
5. Re-attempt automatic rotation
6. Alert security team
```

### ✅ FIX #1: JWT Authentication Implementation
```javascript
// Step 1: Issue tokens via login endpoint
app.post('/login', authLimiter, [...validation...], (req, res) => {
  // Verify credentials
  const token = jwt.sign(
    { id: 1, username: username, role: 'user' },
    process.env.JWT_SECRET,
    { expiresIn: '1h' }
  );
  return res.json({ token });
});

// Step 2: Verify tokens on protected endpoints
const authenticateToken = (req, res, next) => {
  const token = req.headers['authorization']?.split(' ')[1];
  if (!token) return res.status(401).json({ error: 'Access token required' });
  
  jwt.verify(token, process.env.JWT_SECRET, (err, user) => {
    if (err) return res.status(403).json({ error: 'Invalid token' });
    req.user = user;
    next();
  });
};

// Step 3: Protect endpoints
app.get('/users', authenticateToken, authorizeRole(['admin', 'user']), ...);
```

```javascript
];
```

```bash
curl "http://localhost:3000/users?limit=1';DROP TABLE users;--"
# Response: 400 Invalid input
```

```javascript
app.use(helmet());
```

**Headers Added:**
- `Content-Security-Policy` - Prevents XSS
- `X-Frame-Options: DENY` - Prevents clickjacking
- `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` - Prevents MIME sniffing
- `Strict-Transport-Security` - Enforces HTTPS
- `X-XSS-Protection` - Browser XSS protection

```bash

```

```javascript
const limiter = rateLimit({
  windowMs: 15 * 60 * 1000,
  max: 100,
  message: 'Too many requests'
});

  windowMs: 15 * 60 * 1000,
  max: 5,
  message: 'Too many login attempts'
});

app.use(limiter); // General limit
app.post('/login', authLimiter, ...); // Stricter for auth
```

**DOS Protection:**
```bash

for i in {1..10}; do curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/login -d '{}'; done

```

**.gitignore:**

```
node_modules/
*.log
```

**GitHub Integration:**

### ✅ FIX #6: Global Error Handling
```javascript
app.use((err, req, res, next) => {
  console.error('Unhandled error:', err); // Log internally
  
  // Return generic message to client
  const statusCode = err.statusCode || 500;

});
```

**Result:**


```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/login \

  -d '{"username":"demo","password":"demo123456"}'

# 2. Use token to access protected endpoints
curl http://localhost:3000/users \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..."

# Response: { "total": 2, "data": [{ "id": 1, "name": "Alice" }, ...] }
```

---

### ✅ FIX #2: Input Validation with express-validator
```javascript
const validateUserQuery = [
  query('limit')
    .optional()
    .isInt({ min: 1, max: 100 })
    .withMessage('Limit must be between 1 and 100'),
  query('offset')
    .optional()
    .isInt({ min: 0 })
    .withMessage('Offset must be non-negative'),
];

app.get('/users', 
  authenticateToken,
  validateUserQuery,
  handleValidationErrors,
  (req, res) => { ... }
);
```

**Attack Prevention:**
```bash
# Invalid input rejected
curl "http://localhost:3000/users?limit=invalid"
# Response: 400 { "error": "Invalid input", "details": [...] }

# Injection attempt rejected
curl "http://localhost:3000/users?limit={\"$ne\":null}"
# Response: 400 Invalid input

# SQL injection rejected
curl "http://localhost:3000/users?limit=1';DROP TABLE users;--"
# Response: 400 Invalid input
```

---

### ✅ FIX #3: Security Headers with Helmet
```javascript
app.use(helmet());
```

**Headers Added:**
- `Content-Security-Policy` - Prevents XSS
- `X-Frame-Options: DENY` - Prevents clickjacking
- `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` - Prevents MIME sniffing
- `Strict-Transport-Security` - Enforces HTTPS
- `X-XSS-Protection` - Browser XSS protection

**Verification:**
```bash
curl -I http://localhost:3000/health
# X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
# X-Frame-Options: DENY
# Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=15552000; includeSubDomains
```

---

### ✅ FIX #4: Rate Limiting
```javascript
const limiter = rateLimit({
  windowMs: 15 * 60 * 1000,
  max: 100,
  message: 'Too many requests'
});

const authLimiter = rateLimit({
  windowMs: 15 * 60 * 1000,
  max: 5,
  message: 'Too many login attempts'
});

app.use(limiter); // General limit
app.post('/login', authLimiter, ...); // Stricter for auth
```

**DOS Protection:**
```bash
# After 5 attempts on /login
for i in {1..10}; do curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/login -d '{}'; done
# Returns 429 Too Many Requests after attempt 6
```

---

**.gitignore:**
```
.env
.env.local
.env.test
node_modules/
*.log
```

**.env (Never commit):**
```
JWT_SECRET=generate-secure-random-string
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://user:pass@host:5432/db
```

**GitHub Integration:**
- Don't commit .env files
- Use GitHub Secrets for CI/CD
- Use AWS Secrets Manager in production

---

### ✅ FIX #6: Global Error Handling
```javascript
app.use((err, req, res, next) => {
  console.error('Unhandled error:', err); // Log internally
  
  // Return generic message to client
  const statusCode = err.statusCode || 500;
  const message = statusCode === 500 
    ? 'Internal server error' 
    : err.message;
  
  res.status(statusCode).json({ error: message });
});
```

**Result:**
```bash

# Only generic error messages
# Detailed logs available to developers
```

---

```javascript
app.use((req, res, next) => {
  const start = Date.now();
  res.on('finish', () => {
    const duration = Date.now() - start;
    console.log(

    );
  });
  next();
});
```

```

[2024-01-15T10:23:46.456Z] GET /users 200 89ms
```

```javascript
const filteredUsers = users.map(user => {

});
```

```bash
# { "id": 1, "name": "Alice" }
```

**Date:** 2024-01-15

## 🚨 CRITICAL FINDINGS

- **Issue:** Complete absence of authentication/authorization
- **Impact:** All user data exposed publicly without any credentials required
- **Exploitability:** Trivial - Single curl command accesses sensitive data
- **Compliance:** GDPR/CCPA violation - User email addresses exposed as PII
- **Fix Time:** 2-4 hours

  - Database passwords
- **Impact:** Complete system compromise possible
- **Remediation Required:** 
  - ⚠️ **IMMEDIATE:** Rotate all exposed credentials
  - ⚠️ Remove `.env.test` from git history using `git-filter-branch`
  - Add `.env*` to `.gitignore`
- **Fix Time:** 1 hour + credential rotation

### 3. **No Input Validation** - HIGH (CVSS 7.5)
- **Issue:** Zero input validation on all endpoints
- **Risk:** SQL/NoSQL injection, command injection, buffer overflow
- **Current Impact:** Low (endpoints are simple)
- **Future Impact:** High (when more endpoints are added)
- **Fix Time:** 1-2 hours

- **Fix:** Add `helmet.js` middleware
- **Fix Time:** 30 minutes

### 5. **No Rate Limiting** - MEDIUM (CVSS 5.9)

- **Risks:** DOS attacks, brute force attempts, service disruption
- **Fix:** Add `express-rate-limit` middleware
- **Fix Time:** 30 minutes

- **Issue:** Stack traces exposed to clients
- **Risk:** Information disclosure about application architecture
- **Fix:** Implement global error handler
- **Fix Time:** 30 minutes

- **Issue:** Cannot detect or investigate security incidents
- **Risk:** Undetected breaches, forensic blind spot
- **Fix:** Implement request logging and monitoring
- **Fix Time:** 1 hour

- **Risk:** Memory exhaustion, DOS attacks

input.command:
cat > SECURITY_TESTING_GUIDE.md << 'EOF'
# Security Testing Guide for app.js

## Test Cases and Manual Testing Procedures

### 1. AUTHENTICATION TESTING

#### Test 1.1: Unauthenticated Access Blocked
```bash
# Should return 401 Unauthorized
curl -X GET http://localhost:3000/users

# Expected Response:
# { "error": "Access token required" }
```

#### Test 1.2: Invalid Token Rejected
```bash
# Should return 403 Forbidden
curl -X GET http://localhost:3000/users \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer invalid_token_here"

# Expected Response:
# { "error": "Invalid or expired token" }
```

#### Test 1.3: Valid Token Accepted
```bash
# First, login to get a token
TOKEN=$(curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/login \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"username":"alice","password":"password123"}' \
  | jq -r '.token')

# Use token to access protected endpoint
curl -X GET http://localhost:3000/users \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

# Expected Response:
# [
#   { "id": 1, "name": "Alice", "role": "admin" },
#   { "id": 2, "name": "Bob", "role": "user" }
# ]
```

---

### 2. AUTHORIZATION TESTING

#### Test 2.1: Role-Based Access Control
```bash
# Create a non-admin token first (not possible in current simplified app)
# But you can test by modifying JWT payload

# Try accessing admin-only endpoint with non-admin user
# Expected: 403 Forbidden
```

#### Test 2.2: Cross-User Access Prevention
```bash
# Login as Alice (ID: 1)
TOKEN=$(curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/login \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"username":"alice","password":"password123"}' \
  | jq -r '.token')

# Try to access Bob's profile (ID: 2)
curl -X GET http://localhost:3000/users/2 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

# Expected: 403 Forbidden (Unauthorized)
```

---

### 3. INPUT VALIDATION TESTING

#### Test 3.1: Invalid User ID Format
```bash
# Non-numeric ID should be rejected
TOKEN=$(curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/login \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"username":"alice","password":"password123"}' \
  | jq -r '.token')

curl -X GET http://localhost:3000/users/invalid \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

# Expected Response:
# { "errors": [{ "msg": "ID must be an integer", "param": "id" }] }
```

#### Test 3.2: Login Input Validation - Short Password
```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/login \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"username":"alice","password":"short"}'

# Expected: 400 Bad Request with validation error
```

#### Test 3.3: Login Input Validation - Missing Fields
```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/login \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"username":"alice"}'

# Expected: 400 Bad Request
```

---

### 4. RATE LIMITING TESTING

#### Test 4.1: General Rate Limit
```bash
# Make 100+ requests in quick succession
for i in {1..105}; do
  curl -X GET http://localhost:3000/health
done

# After 100 requests, subsequent requests should return 429 Too Many Requests
```

#### Test 4.2: Strict Rate Limit on Login
```bash
# Make 5+ failed login attempts
for i in {1..6}; do
  curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/login \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"username":"attacker","password":"wrong"}'
done

# 6th attempt should return 429 Too Many Requests
```

---

### 5. CORS TESTING

#### Test 5.1: Valid Origin Allowed
```bash
curl -X GET http://localhost:3000/health \
  -H "Origin: http://localhost:3000"

# Should include CORS headers:
# access-control-allow-origin: http://localhost:3000
```

#### Test 5.2: Invalid Origin Blocked
```bash
curl -X GET http://localhost:3000/health \
  -H "Origin: http://malicious-site.com"

# Should return 403 or not include CORS headers
```

#### Test 5.3: Preflight Request
```bash
curl -X OPTIONS http://localhost:3000/users \
  -H "Origin: http://localhost:3000" \
  -H "Access-Control-Request-Method: POST" \
  -H "Access-Control-Request-Headers: Content-Type"

# Should return 200 with appropriate CORS headers
```

---

### 6. REQUEST SIZE TESTING

#### Test 6.1: Oversized Payload
```bash
# Create a large payload (> 10kb)
python3 -c "
import json
import requests
large_data = {'data': 'x' * 20000}
response = requests.post('http://localhost:3000/login', json=large_data)
print(response.status_code)
"

# Should return 413 Payload Too Large
```

---

### 7. SECURITY HEADERS TESTING

#### Test 7.1: Check Security Headers
```bash
curl -I http://localhost:3000/health

# Should include:
# X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
# X-Frame-Options: DENY
# X-XSS-Protection: 1; mode=block
# Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000
# Content-Security-Policy: ...
```

---

### 8. HTTPS ENFORCEMENT TESTING (Production)

#### Test 8.1: HTTP Redirect
```bash
# In production, should redirect HTTP to HTTPS
curl -i http://yourdomain.com/health

# Should return 301 redirect to https://yourdomain.com/health
```

---

### 9. ERROR HANDLING TESTING

#### Test 9.1: Production Error Messages
```bash
# Set NODE_ENV=production
export NODE_ENV=production

# Trigger an error
curl -X GET http://localhost:3000/invalid-endpoint

# Should NOT expose stack trace or internal details
# Response: { "error": "Not found" }
```

#### Test 9.2: Development Error Messages
```bash
# Set NODE_ENV=development
export NODE_ENV=development

# Trigger an error
curl -X GET http://localhost:3000/invalid-endpoint

# May include more detailed error information
```

---

### 10. INJECTION ATTACK TESTING

#### Test 10.1: SQL Injection Attempt (if database queries added)
```bash
# Example malicious input
curl -X GET "http://localhost:3000/users/1' OR '1'='1" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

# With parameterized queries: Safe (returns validation error)
# Without parameterized queries: Vulnerable to injection
```

#### Test 10.2: XSS Payload in Login
```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/login \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"username":"<script>alert(1)</script>","password":"test123456"}'

# Should sanitize/escape the input before processing
# Or with .escape() in express-validator, should be safe
```

---

### 11. ENVIRONMENT VARIABLE TESTING

#### Test 11.1: Missing JWT_SECRET in Production
```bash
# Start app in production without JWT_SECRET
NODE_ENV=production node app.js

# Should throw error: "JWT_SECRET environment variable is required in production"
```

---

### 12. LOGGING & MONITORING TESTING

#### Test 12.1: Security Events Logged
```bash
# Perform a failed login
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/login \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"username":"attacker","password":"wrong"}'

# Check logs for:
# [SECURITY] Failed login attempt with IP logged
```

#### Test 12.2: Unauthorized Access Logged
```bash
# Try to access admin endpoint as non-admin
# Check logs for:
# [SECURITY] Authorization denied
```

---

## Automated Security Testing

### Using OWASP ZAP
```bash
# Start OWASP ZAP
docker run -t owasp/zap2docker-stable zap-baseline.py \
  -t http://localhost:3000

# Or full scan
docker run -t owasp/zap2docker-stable zap-full-scan.py \
  -t http://localhost:3000 \
  -r report.html
```

### Using npm audit
```bash
npm audit
npm audit fix
```

### Using Snyk
```bash
npm install -g snyk
snyk test
snyk monitor
```

---

## Testing Checklist

- [ ] All endpoints require authentication (except /health and /login)
- [ ] Invalid tokens are rejected
- [ ] Expired tokens are rejected
- [ ] Rate limiting is enforced
- [ ] CORS only allows configured origins
- [ ] Input validation prevents injection attacks
- [ ] Oversized payloads are rejected
- [ ] Security headers are present
- [ ] Error messages don't leak sensitive info in production
- [ ] Failed login attempts are logged
- [ ] Unauthorized access attempts are logged
- [ ] HTTPS is enforced in production
- [ ] Environment variables are properly validated

EOF
cat SECURITY_TESTING_GUIDE.md

```bash
response = requests.post('http://localhost:3000/login', json=large_data)
print(response.status_code)
"

# Should return 413 Payload Too Large
```

---

### 7. SECURITY HEADERS TESTING

#### Test 7.1: Check Security Headers
```bash
curl -I http://localhost:3000/health

# Should include:
# X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
# X-Frame-Options: DENY
# X-XSS-Protection: 1; mode=block
# Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000
# Content-Security-Policy: ...
```

---

### 8. HTTPS ENFORCEMENT TESTING (Production)

#### Test 8.1: HTTP Redirect
```bash
# In production, should redirect HTTP to HTTPS
curl -i http://yourdomain.com/health

# Should return 301 redirect to https://yourdomain.com/health
```

---

### 9. ERROR HANDLING TESTING

#### Test 9.1: Production Error Messages
```bash
# Set NODE_ENV=production
export NODE_ENV=production

# Trigger an error
curl -X GET http://localhost:3000/invalid-endpoint

# Should NOT expose stack trace or internal details
# Response: { "error": "Not found" }
```

#### Test 9.2: Development Error Messages
```bash
# Set NODE_ENV=development
export NODE_ENV=development

# Trigger an error
curl -X GET http://localhost:3000/invalid-endpoint

# May include more detailed error information
```

---

### 10. INJECTION ATTACK TESTING

#### Test 10.1: SQL Injection Attempt (if database queries added)
```bash
# Example malicious input
curl -X GET "http://localhost:3000/users/1' OR '1'='1" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

# With parameterized queries: Safe (returns validation error)
# Without parameterized queries: Vulnerable to injection
```

#### Test 10.2: XSS Payload in Login
```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/login \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"username":"<script>alert(1)</script>","password":"test123456"}'

# Should sanitize/escape the input before processing
# Or with .escape() in express-validator, should be safe
```

---

### 11. ENVIRONMENT VARIABLE TESTING

#### Test 11.1: Missing JWT_SECRET in Production
```bash
# Start app in production without JWT_SECRET
NODE_ENV=production node app.js

# Should throw error: "JWT_SECRET environment variable is required in production"
```

---

### 12. LOGGING & MONITORING TESTING

#### Test 12.1: Security Events Logged
```bash
# Perform a failed login
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/login \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"username":"attacker","password":"wrong"}'

# Check logs for:
# [SECURITY] Failed login attempt with IP logged
```

#### Test 12.2: Unauthorized Access Logged
```bash
# Try to access admin endpoint as non-admin
# Check logs for:
# [SECURITY] Authorization denied
```

---

## Automated Security Testing

### Using OWASP ZAP
```bash
# Start OWASP ZAP
docker run -t owasp/zap2docker-stable zap-baseline.py \
  -t http://localhost:3000

# Or full scan
docker run -t owasp/zap2docker-stable zap-full-scan.py \
  -t http://localhost:3000 \
  -r report.html
```

### Using npm audit
```bash
npm audit
npm audit fix
```

### Using Snyk
```bash
npm install -g snyk
snyk test
snyk monitor
```

---

## Testing Checklist

- [ ] All endpoints require authentication (except /health and /login)
- [ ] Invalid tokens are rejected
- [ ] Expired tokens are rejected
- [ ] Rate limiting is enforced
- [ ] CORS only allows configured origins
- [ ] Input validation prevents injection attacks
- [ ] Oversized payloads are rejected
- [ ] Security headers are present
- [ ] Error messages don't leak sensitive info in production
- [ ] Failed login attempts are logged
- [ ] Unauthorized access attempts are logged
- [ ] HTTPS is enforced in production
- [ ] Environment variables are properly validated

/**
 * Pre-commit hook to prevent secrets from being committed
 * Install in .git/hooks/pre-commit and make executable
 * 
 * chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
 */

#!/bin/bash

set -e

# Colors for output
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

echo -e "${YELLOW}🔐 Running pre-commit security checks...${NC}"

# Check for staged .env files
if git diff --cached --name-only | grep -E "\.env($|\.)" >/dev/null; then
  echo -e "${RED}❌ ERROR: .env files should not be committed${NC}"
  echo "Staged .env files:"
  git diff --cached --name-only | grep -E "\.env($|\.)"
  exit 1
fi

# Check for secret patterns in staged files
echo -e "${YELLOW}Scanning for secret patterns...${NC}"

# Common patterns to detect
PATTERNS=(
  "AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}"  # AWS Access Keys
  "sk_live_[0-9a-zA-Z]{20,}"  # Stripe Live Keys
  "sk-ant-[0-9a-zA-Z]{20,}"  # Anthropic Keys
  "password\s*[:=]\s*['\"][^'\"]{5,}['\"]"  # Password assignments
  "secret\s*[:=]\s*['\"][^'\"]{10,}['\"]"  # Secret assignments
  "token\s*[:=]\s*['\"][^'\"]{20,}['\"]"  # Token assignments
)

FOUND_SECRETS=0

for file in $(git diff --cached --name-only); do
  if [[ ! -d "$file" ]]; then
    for pattern in "${PATTERNS[@]}"; do
      if grep -E "$pattern" "$file" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo -e "${RED}⚠️  Potential secret found in: $file${NC}"
        echo "   Pattern: $pattern"
        FOUND_SECRETS=1
      fi
    done
  fi
done

if [ $FOUND_SECRETS -eq 1 ]; then
  echo -e "${RED}❌ ERROR: Potential secrets detected in staged files${NC}"
  echo "Please remove sensitive data before committing"
  exit 1
fi

# Check for common secret file extensions
if git diff --cached --name-only | grep -E "\.(key|pem|p12|pfx|jks)$" >/dev/null; then
  echo -e "${RED}❌ ERROR: Private key files detected${NC}"
  exit 1
fi

echo -e "${GREEN}✅ Pre-commit checks passed${NC}"
exit 0

        with:

          head: HEAD
          extra_args: --debug

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

        run: |

      - name: Scan for AWS credentials
        run: |
          git secrets --install
          git secrets --register-aws
          git secrets --scan

  # Dependency security scanning
  dependency-scan:
    name: NPM Dependency Audit
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

        with:

```javascript
const AWS = require('aws-sdk');
```
